_readme: Level 2 Tax Code Book leaves (LevelBookLeaves). They appear after the shared book's three sections in Office_Level2 only; Level 1's book is unchanged. In Level 2 the book first opens on the first leaf below.

Sections 4-6 are reference pages for Mark the Money! and the office review: each term is printed like the shared pages' values (readOnly: true, so it cannot be picked up) with its explanation underneath. Sections 7-8 hold the selectable finding reasons and conclusions.
A leaf whose body has one paragraph (blank-line separated) per value prints each paragraph under its value; keep those counts equal.
Leaves explain concepts. Never put a client's amounts, a finding, the summary answer or the stamp to choose here.

Simplified classroom rules, not legal advice. The loan-principal rule is an EDUCATIONAL DRAFT: no confirmed Philippine primary-source passage yet (see Documentation/Level2SomethingDoesNotMatch/CONTENT.md).
Fields starting with '_' are notes and are ignored by the game.

sections.heading: Section 4 – Income Types
sections.body:
Pay from an employer for work done as an employee.

Payment for your own trade or for a job done for a customer.

Payment for letting someone use your property.

Earnings from money or investments, such as bank interest. Check its own rule first.

Money that must be paid back. Borrowing is not earning.

sections.heading: Section 5 – Income Treatment
sections.body:
Earned income, listed with the other income of the same period.

Income that follows its own rule instead of the regular schedule.

Only for items a law itself excludes.

Money that was never earned, such as a loan that must be repaid. An educational simplification.

sections.heading: Section 6 – Checking a Summary
sections.body:
Match each line the summary lists with the record behind it.

An earned payment with no summary line. Add it once, in its month.

Money arriving in the bank is not proof it was earned. Read why it arrived.

The one record written for that payment. Your annotated papers already hold it.

sections.heading: Section 7 – Finding Reasons
sections.body:
A monthly sum should include every earned payment for that month, including separate jobs.

A difference matters when dates and scope match.

A deposit may be borrowed money, rather than pay.

sections.heading: Section 8 – Review Conclusions
sections.body:
The record confirms an earned payment belongs in this period, so you added it.

The records explain the difference; no change is needed.

The difference still needs investigation.
